'''Martin Andreas Nowak''' (born April 7, 1965)<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |title=SuperCooperators: altruism, evolution, and why we need each other to succeed |last2=Highfield |first2=Roger |date=2012 |publisher=Free Press |isbn=978-1-4516-2663-6 |edition=1. Free Press trade paperback |location=New York, NY}}</ref><ref name="Wax" /> is an Austrian-born professor of mathematics and biology at [[Harvard University]]. He is known for his work in [[evolutionary dynamics]], focusing on evolutionary theory and viral dynamics.<ref name="Wax">{{cite news |last=Wax |first=Heather |date=October 15, 2007 |title=Cooperation counts for math professor |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110703034711/https://www.boston.com/yourlife/health/articles/2007/10/15/cooperation_counts_for_math_professor/ |url=http://archive.boston.com/news/globe/health_science/articles/2007/10/15/cooperation_counts_for_math_professor/ |url-status=live |archive-date=July 3, 2011 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[The Boston Globe]] |quote= Nowak, 42, a Harvard University mathematician and biologist, is at the forefront of a new field called evolutionary dynamics, in which Darwin's idea of natural selection is formulated in terms of math equations.}}</ref>

Nowak held faculty positions at [[Oxford University]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton]], before beginning a post at Harvard in July 2003.

Nowak was one of the primary recipients of funding from child sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]] to Harvard faculty,<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=Marks |first1=Stephen M. |last2=Schuker |first2=Lauren A. E. |date=February 7, 2003 |title=Magnate donates $30M to sciences |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2003/2/7/magnate-donates-30m-to-sciences-an/|website=[[The Harvard Crimson]]}},</ref> and Epstein left Nowak US$5,000,000 in his trust. He was placed on paid administrative leave by Harvard twice in response to his dealings with Epstein, first in 2021, and then in February 2026.<ref name="Admin Leave">{{cite web |last1=Marks |first1=Jonathan |last2=Shaw|date=February 27, 2026 |title=Martin Nowak Placed on Leave a Second Time |url = https://www.harvardmagazine.com/university-news/martin-nowak-harvard-administrative-leave-epstein|website =The Harvard Crimson}}</ref>

In March 2026 he resigned from the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-26 |title=Mathematiker Nowak scheidet aus ÖAW aus |url=https://science.orf.at/stories/3234807/ |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=science.ORF.at |language=de}}</ref><ref name="o943">{{cite web | title=Martin Nowak resigns from Austrian Academy of Sciences membership | website=Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften | url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/news/martin-nowak-resigns-from-austrian-academy-of-sciences-membership }}</ref><ref name="i087">{{cite web | title=Harvard Professor Martin Nowak Resigns From Austrian Academy Amid Epstein Scrutiny | website=The Harvard Crimson | date=2026-02-25 | url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2026/4/2/nowak-austrian-academy-resignation/}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Nowak was born in [[Vienna]], Austria, on April 7, 1965.<ref name="Wax" /> He studied at the {{ill|Albertus Magnus Gymnasium in Vienna|de|Albertus-Magnus-Schule Wien}} and the [[University of Vienna]], where he earned a doctorate in biochemistry and mathematics in 1989. During his studies, he collaborated with [[Peter Schuster (theoretical chemist)|Peter Schuster]] on [[Quasispecies model|quasispecies theory]] and with [[Karl Sigmund]] on the evolution of cooperation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nowak |first=Martin |title=Evolution of cooperation |url=https://web.mit.edu/9.s915/www/classes/slides_nowak.pdf |access-date=June 20, 2025 |website=MIT}}</ref> Nowak received the Sub auspiciis Praesidentis award upon completing his doctorate at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Witzmann|first=Erich|date=2011-04-03|title=Martin Nowak: "Junge sollen unabhängig forschen"|url=https://www.diepresse.com/647277/martin-nowak-junge-sollen-unabhangig-forschen|access-date=2020-06-08|website=Die Presse|language=de}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

==Career==
In 1989, Nowak worked at the [[University of Oxford]] with [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford|Robert May]] as an [[Erwin Schrödinger]] Postdoctoral Scholar. He later became a [[Junior Research Fellowships|Junior Research Fellow]] at [[Wolfson College, Oxford|Wolfson College]] and then [[Keble College]]. In 1992, he became a [[Wellcome Trust]] Senior Research Fellow in Biomedical Science<ref name=paynerj>{{cite journal |last1=Payne |first1=R J |last2=Nowak |first2=M A |last3=Blumberg |first3=B S |title=The dynamics of hepatitis B virus infection. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=25 June 1996 |volume=93 |issue=13 |pages=6542–6546 |doi=10.1073/pnas.93.13.6542 |pmid=8692852 |bibcode=1996PNAS...93.6542P |doi-access=free |pmc=39060 }}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref> before becoming a professor of Mathematical Biology in 1997.<ref name=nowak_sigmund>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=Sigmund |first2=Karl |title=Evolution of indirect reciprocity by image scoring |journal=Nature |date=June 1998 |volume=393 |issue=6685 |pages=573–577 |doi=10.1038/31225 |pmid=9634232 |bibcode=1998Natur.393..573N |s2cid=4395576 }}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref>

In 1998, Nowak became the head of the Program in Theoretical Biology at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dyson |first=Freeman J. |date=2019-12-09 |title=Martin Nowak - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/martin-nowak |access-date=2025-07-31 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> In 2003, he became a professor of mathematics and biology at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=University Lures Specialist In Interdisciplinary Science |newspaper= The Harvard Crimson|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2002/10/1/university-lures-specialist-in-interdisciplinary-science/|first=Christina M. |last=Anderson |date=2002-10-01|access-date=2020-10-10}}</ref> Nowak was also a co-director, with [[Sarah Coakley]], of the Evolution and Theology of Cooperation project at Harvard, sponsored by the [[Templeton Foundation]],<ref>[http://www.fas.harvard.edu/~etc/index.html Evolution and Theology of Cooperation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> where he was also a member of its Board of Advisors.<ref>[http://www.templeton.org/about_us/who_we_are/board_of_advisors/ About Us : Who We Are : Board of Advisors<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070123171823/http://www.templeton.org/about_us/who_we_are/board_of_advisors/ |date=2007-01-23 }}</ref>

Nowak's research focuses on [[evolutionary game theory]], [[cancer]], [[virus]]es, [[infectious disease]], the [[Evolutionary linguistics|evolution of language]] and the [[evolution of cooperation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=M.A. |year=2006 |title=Five rules for the evolution of cooperation |journal=Science |volume=314 |issue=5805 |pages=1560–1563 |bibcode=2006Sci...314.1560N |doi=10.1126/science.1133755 |pmc=3279745 |pmid=17158317}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wei |first1=X. |last2=Ghosh |first2=S.K. |last3=Taylor |first3=M.E. |last4=Nowak |first4=M.A. |last5=Hahn |first5=B.H. |last6=Saag |first6=M.S. |last7=Shaw |first7=G.M. |year=1995 |title=Viral dynamics in human immunodeficiency virus type 1 infection |journal=Nature |volume=373 |issue=6510 |pages=117–122 |bibcode=1995Natur.373..117W |doi=10.1038/373117a0 |pmid=7529365 |s2cid=4343212}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=M.A. |last2=May |first2=R.M. |year=2018 |title=Minimal functional driver gene heterogeneity among untreated metastases |journal=Science |volume=361 |issue=6406 |pages=1033–1037 |bibcode=1992Natur.359..826N |doi=10.1038/359826a0 |pmc=6329287 |pmid=30190408}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite book |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin |title=Evolutionary Dynamics: Exploring the Equations of Life |date=October 2006 |publisher=[[Harvard University Press|Belknap Press]] |isbn=978-0-674-02338-3}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=J.B. |last2=Shen |first2=Y.K. |last3=Aiden |first3=A.P. |last4=Nowak |first4=M.A. |last5=Aiden |first5=E.L. |year=2011 |title=Quantitative analysis of culture using millions of digitized books |journal=Science |volume=331 |issue=6014 |pages=176–182 |bibcode=1992Natur.359..826N |doi=10.1038/359826a0 |pmc=3279742 |pmid=21163965}}</ref> At Oxford, he helped to establish the fields of virus dynamics<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=Anderson |first2=Roy M. |last3=McLean |first3=Angela R. |last4=Wolfs |first4=Tom F. W. |last5=Goudsmit |first5=Jaap |last6=May |first6=Robert M. |date=15 November 1991 |title=Antigenic Diversity Thresholds and the Development of AIDS |journal=Science |volume=254 |issue=5034 |pages=963–969 |bibcode=1991Sci...254..963N |doi=10.1126/science.1683006 |pmid=1683006}}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref> and spatial games<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=May |first2=Robert M. |date=October 1992 |title=Evolutionary games and spatial chaos |journal=Nature |volume=359 |issue=6398 |pages=826–829 |bibcode=1992Natur.359..826N |doi=10.1038/359826a0 |s2cid=4328667}}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref> (which later became evolutionary graph theory). He has collaborated with [[John Maynard Smith]] on genetic redundancy,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=Boerlijst |first2=Maarten C. |last3=Cooke |first3=Jonathan |last4=Smith |first4=John Maynard |date=July 1997 |title=Evolution of genetic redundancy |journal=Nature |volume=388 |issue=6638 |pages=167–171 |bibcode=1997Natur.388..167N |doi=10.1038/40618 |pmid=9217155 |doi-access=free}}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref> [[Baruch Blumberg]] on the [[hepatitis B virus]],<ref name="paynerj" /> [[Karl Sigmund]] on game theory,<ref name="nowak_sigmund" /> and with George Shaw and [[Andrew McMichael]] on [[HIV]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wei |first1=Xiping |last2=Ghosh |first2=Sajal K. |last3=Taylor |first3=Maria E. |last4=Johnson |first4=Victoria A. |last5=Emini |first5=Emilio A. |last6=Deutsch |first6=Paul |last7=Lifson |first7=Jeffrey D. |last8=Bonhoeffer |first8=Sebastian |last9=Nowak |first9=Martin A. |last10=Hahn |first10=Beatrice H. |last11=Saag |first11=Michael S. |last12=Shaw |first12=George M. |date=January 1995 |title=Viral dynamics in human immunodeficiency virus type 1 infection |journal=Nature |volume=373 |issue=6510 |pages=117–122 |bibcode=1995Natur.373..117W |doi=10.1038/373117a0 |pmid=7529365 |s2cid=4343212}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=McMichael |first2=Andrew J. |date=August 1995 |title=How HIV Defeats the Immune System |journal=Scientific American |volume=273 |issue=2 |pages=58–65 |bibcode=1995SciAm.273b..58N |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0895-58 |pmid=7652527}}{{primary source inline|date=February 2024}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Eigen |first1=M. |last2=Nieselt-Struwe |first2=K. |year=1990 |title=How old is the immunodeficiency virus? |journal=AIDS |volume=4 |pages=S95–7 |doi=10.1097/00002030-199001001-00014 |pmid=2152591}}</ref>

He has published several books on evolutionary dynamics,<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |title=Virus dynamics - Martin A. Nowak; Robert May - Oxford University Press |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/virus-dynamics-9780198504177 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240108072004/https://global.oup.com/academic/product/virus-dynamics-9780198504177?cc=us&lang=en& |archive-date=January 8, 2024 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nee |first1=Sean |author-link1=Sean Nee |date=November 1, 2006 |title=Beautiful models |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/444037a |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=444 |issue=7115 |page=37 |bibcode=2006Natur.444...37N |doi=10.1038/444037a |url-access=subscription |access-date=January 8, 2024}}</ref>  the evolution of cooperation,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harman |first1=Oren |author-link1=Oren Harman |date=April 8, 2011 |title=How Evolution Explains Altruism |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/04/10/books/review/book-review-supercooperators-by-martin-a-nowak.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214235126/https://www.nytimes.com/2011/04/10/books/review/book-review-supercooperators-by-martin-a-nowak.html |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |title=Evolution, Games, and God — Harvard University Press |url=https://www.hup.harvard.edu/books/9780674047976 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240108080751/https://www.hup.harvard.edu/books/9780674047976 |archive-date=January 8, 2024 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[Harvard University Press]]}}</ref> and religion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-27 |title=Beyond |url=http://www.martinnowak.com/books/beyond |access-date=2025-07-31 |website=Martin Nowak |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Opposition to inclusive fitness theory===
{{See also|Inclusive fitness#Opposing view|Kin selection#Objections}}
Nowak is a noted critic of inclusive fitness theory, and in 2010 published a paper along with [[Corina Tarnita]] and [[E. O. Wilson]] on the subject.<ref name=NTW>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=Martin A. |last2=Tarnita |first2=Corina E. |last3=Wilson |first3=Edward O. |author3-link=Edward O. Wilson |title=The evolution of eusociality |journal=Nature |volume=466 |issue=7310 |pages=1057–1062 |doi=10.1038/nature09205 |pmid=20740005 |pmc=3279739 |year=2010 |bibcode=2010Natur.466.1057N |author1-link=Martin Nowak }}</ref>
A letter stating that Nowak's paper did not accurately represent inclusive fitness theory was co-signed by 137 authors and published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name="137 authors reply to Nowak 2011">{{cite journal |last1=Abbot |first1=Patrick |last2=Abe |first2=Jun |last3=Alcock |first3=John |last4=Alizon |first4=Samuel |last5=Alpedrinha |first5=Joao A. In 2016, Nowak and Benjamin Allen published further work critical of inclusive fitness theory.<ref name="v036">{{cite journal | last1=Allen | first1=Benjamin | last2=Nowak | first2=Martin A | title=There is no inclusive fitness at the level of the individual | journal=Current Opinion in Behavioral Sciences | volume=12 | date=2016 | doi=10.1016/j.cobeha.2016.10.002 | pages=122–128 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S2352154616301966 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
[[Jonathan Birch (philosopher)|Jonathan Birch]] wrote in 2017 that there was "still little evidence of any serious reconciliation" between the two views.<ref name="c718">{{cite journal | last=Birch | first=Jonathan | title=The inclusive fitness controversy: finding a way forward | journal=Royal Society Open Science | volume=4 | issue=7 | date=2017 | issn=2054-5703 | pmid=28791162 | pmc=5541557 | doi=10.1098/rsos.170335 | article-number=170335 | doi-access=free | bibcode=2017RSOS....470335B }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Nowak is a [[Roman Catholic]].<ref name="discover">{{cite news |last1=Ohlson |first1=Kristin |title=The Cooperation Instinct |url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/planet-earth/the-cooperation-instinct |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604143639/https://www.discovermagazine.com/planet-earth/the-cooperation-instinct |url-status=live |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]] |date=October 25, 2012 |archive-date=June 4, 2023}}</ref> In a 2007 lecture at Harvard, he argued that science and religion occupied different but complementary roles in humans' search for meaning, stating: "Science and religion are two essential components in the search for truth. Denying either is a barren approach."<ref name="Gazette">{{cite news |last1=Powell |first1=Alvin |title=Can science, religion coexist in peace? |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2007/03/can-science-religion-coexist-in-peace/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230922055027/https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2007/03/can-science-religion-coexist-in-peace/ |url-status=live |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[The Harvard Gazette]] |date=March 15, 2007 |archive-date=September 22, 2023}}</ref>

== Relationship with Jeffrey Epstein ==
Nowak maintained a close personal and financial relationship with the financier and convicted sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Professors Who Stayed Close With Epstein|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/21/us/professors-jeffrey-epstein-relationships.html|work=The New York Times|date=2025-11-21|access-date=2026-01-31|issn=0362-4331|language=en-US|first1=Mark ArsenaultChris|last1=Hippensteel|first2=Danny|last2=Hakim}}</ref> The preface of his 2006 textbook, ''Evolutionary Dynamics: Exploring the Equations of Life'', ends with "I thank Jeffrey Epstein for many ideas and for letting me participate in his passionate pursuit of knowledge in all its forms."<ref>{{cite book |last=Nowak |first=Martin A. |title=Evolutionary Dynamics: Exploring the Equations of Life |publisher=Belknap Press of Harvard University Press |year=2006 |chapter=Preface |pages=ix–xiv |doi=10.2307/j.ctvjghw98.3 |jstor=j.ctvjghw98.3 |isbn=978-0-674-02338-3 }}</ref>

In response to the revelations of Epstein's support of Nowak and his lab (the Program for Evolutionary Dynamics), in 2021 Nowak was suspended from supervising undergraduate research for two years, and the institute was permanently closed.<ref name="harvmag">{{cite web |last1=Gibson|first1=Lydialyle|date=March 25, 2021|title=Martin Nowak sanctioned for Jeffrey Epstein involvement|url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2021/03/martin-nowak-sanctioned-for-jeffrey-epstein-involvement|website=[[Harvard Magazine]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Helmore|first1=Edward|date=March 27, 2021|title=Harvard closes evolution center after finding connections to Jeffrey Epstein|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/mar/27/harvard-closes-evolution-center-after-finding-connections-jeffrey-epstein|website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Harvard's review, leading to the suspension, uncovered that Epstein had maintained access to a personal office in Nowak's lab for nine years, even after his conviction for [[sex crimes]], and used the office over 40 times, "typically accompanied by young women serving as his assistants".<ref>{{cite news|date=May 1, 2020|first1=Susan|title=Jeffrey Epstein had his own office at Harvard University — after he was convicted as a sex offender|last1=Svrluga|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2020/05/01/jeffrey-epstein-harvard-report/}}</ref> Additionally, Nowak made contact with Epstein at least 150 times after his conviction, helping set up meetings with Harvard professors who Epstein used to connect with academics, politicians, and other guests.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chiasson |first1=Hugo C. |last2=Spenner |first2=Elise A. |date=February 25, 2026 |title=Harvard Places Math Professor Martin Nowak on Paid Administrative Leave Over Epstein Ties |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2026/2/25/nowak-leave-epstein/ |access-date=May 14, 2026 |work=The Harvard Crimson}}</ref>

In 2023, Harvard lifted the sanctions against Nowak, and he remains on the faculty, jointly appointed in the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Harvard Lifted Sanctions on Epstein-Associated Professor Martin Nowak in March {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2023/5/22/nowak-sanctions-lifted/|access-date=2025-09-14|website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref>

On February 25, 2026, Harvard announced that Nowak had been placed on administrative leave from the university after a formal investigation was opened by the Faculty of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/25/us/larry-summers-resignation-harvard-epstein.html |title=Lawrence Summers Will Resign From Harvard After Epstein Revelations|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=2024-05-26}}</ref>

Epstein left Nowak {{Currency|5 million|USD}} in his [[Trust (law)|trust]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldstein |first=Matthew |date=2026-02-03 |title=Epstein's Trust Reveals Who Would Inherit His Fortune |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/03/business/jeffrey-epstein-trust-inherit-karyna-shuliak.html |access-date=2026-02-18 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
